sovereign_country.strategic_role: 苏伊士运河经济特区、辐射中东及北非的低成本轻工制造

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Programmatic Real-Time Ad Exchange and SSP Platform

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended (Articles 102–123 governing Limited Liability Companies); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations; relevant registration provisions of the Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Foreign Trade (GAFI) — Company Registration One-Stop Shop, and the Commercial Registry Authority of the Ministry of Trade and Industry
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (Incorporation Contract) filed together with GAFI Statutory Incorporation Application Form No. 1
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an LLC under Law 159/1981; however, the capital must be fully subscribed, adequate for the declared business purpose, deposited to a temporary bank account opened in the company's name, with an irrevocable bank certificate submitted at incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that all subscribed shares in the capital of the Company, as set out in the duly notarized Memorandum of Association, are hereby confirmed as fully subscribed and allotted to the founding shareholders. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at the address stated in the Memorandum, and such address is adopted as the Company's statutory seat in the Arab Republic of Egypt. RESOLVED, that the founding directors are hereby appointed as the first officers, vested with full authority to represent the Company before GAFI, the Commercial Registry, banks, and tax authorities, to open bank accounts, and to perfect all incorporation formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Trade Name Reservation and Legal Form Validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (Companies Affairs Department) and Commercial Registry name-search window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three alternative trade names in the required LLC format, verify compliance with naming restrictions under Law 159/1981, obtain the name availability certificate, and obtain pre-approval of the LLC corporate form for foreign-owned digital services.
required_dossiers: Signed name reservation request form
Copies of founding shareholders' passports or national ID cards
Notarized power of attorney (if an incorporation agent or lawyer is appointed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the first proposed name is rejected, the applicant may automatically proceed to the second or third alternative name without additional fees; a written appeal against refusal can be filed with the GAFI Corporate Form Committee within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cairo Notary Public Office and GAFI Legal Affairs Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the incorporation contract before a public notary; all shareholders must sign physically or by certified electronic signature under the Electronic Signature Law No. 15 of 2004; pay notarial stamp duties and obtain the notarization seal prior to filing.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Trade name reservation certificate
Shareholders' passport or national ID copies
Proof of registered office lease or ownership title
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notarial deficiencies, such as missing signatures or insufficient stamp duties, may be cured by resubmitting corrected signature pages within 30 days; re-notarization fees are waived where the error is attributable to the notary office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Issuance of the Bank Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary joint bank account in the intended company name, deposit the fully subscribed paid-up capital via Swift/Wire or ACH inbound remittance from shareholders' foreign accounts, and obtain the irrevocable capital deposit certificate required for incorporation.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum of Association
GAFI pre-approval certificate
Shareholders' identification documents and proof of source of funds
Bank AML/KYC forms and economic sanctions declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the source of funds, the corporate secretary must submit a statutory declaration and supporting bank statements to the CBE Financial Intelligence Unit within 7 days; upon clearance the deposit certificate is released, otherwise the account is closed with a full refund.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation Application and Issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop, Cairo Headquarters or Governorate Branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete incorporation application through the GAFI electronic portal, attach the notarized memorandum, capital deposit certificate, registered-office lease contract (minimum one-year term), and first board resolution; pay the statutory fees and receive the Certificate of Incorporation and company registration number.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation application form (Form No. 1)
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Bank capital deposit certificate
Certified copy of the first board resolution
Registered office lease contract
Passport copies of all shareholders and directors
Good-conduct certificates for each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: GAFI may issue a deficiency memorandum listing the defects; the applicant is entitled to cure within 30 days by submitting supplementary documents and revised forms; administrative refusal may be appealed before the GAFI Investment Disputes Resolution Committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Registration and Issuance of the Trade Register Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Office of the Ministry of Trade and Industry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon GAFI approval, deposit the incorporation dossier with the Commercial Registry office having territorial jurisdiction, obtain the trade register extract (commercial registration certificate), and initiate the mandatory publication procedure.
required_dossiers: GAFI certificate of incorporation
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Business activity statement under ISIC 7310 and NAICS 541810
Identification and status verification of company officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects the application due to an activity-classification mismatch, the company shall file an amended business-activity statement aligned to ISIC 7310 and reapply within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Card and Value-Added Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — Corporate Income Tax and VAT Departments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the tax card (taxpayer registration certificate) and register for VAT on the taxable supply of programmatic advertising exchange and SSP services; disclose the inbound payment rails (Swift Wire, ACH Direct) and obtain unified tax identification numbers for corporate tax and VAT purposes.
required_dossiers: Commercial registry certificate
Certificate of incorporation
Registered office lease contract and utility bill
Directors' passport and ID copies
Projected revenue declaration and payment-rail disclosure statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried due to non-resident ownership, the company shall file residency certificates of shareholders and applicable double-taxation treaty declarations; a written response to the ETA remedial request must be submitted within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer with NOSI, submit the payroll structure and planned employee roster for Egyptian and foreign staff, and obtain the employer registration number for monthly social insurance contributions.
required_dossiers: Commercial registry certificate
Tax card
Employer registration declaration form
Scheduled employee roster and contract templates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Objections to the NOSI classification of employees or contribution rates are submitted to the NOSI Appeals Committee; penalties for under-declaration may be mitigated by voluntary disclosure within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating License and Civil Defense Clearance for the Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Municipality Licensing Office and Civil Defense Directorate of the Ministry of Interior
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the municipal operating license for office-based digital-services premises, install approved fire-fighting and emergency-safety equipment, pass the structural-load and safety inspection, and receive the Civil Defense clearance certificate before commencing physical operations.
required_dossiers: Commercial registry certificate
Registered office lease contract and municipality fee receipt
Civil defense application form
Fire-safety installation report by an approved engineer
Floor plan of the registered office premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality requires structural modifications or additional fire-safety measures, the company shall submit an amended floor plan and accredited engineering certificate; a re-inspection is scheduled within 7 working days after the defects are remedied.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) — not applicable; the undertaking is a non-industrial digital advertising exchange and SSP platform with no manufacturing or physical production facility
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Commercial Operating License for Service Offices (Rekhsa); no industrial or technical manufacturing license applies to the AdTech activity

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C — Exempt from full EIA screening; office-based computer and data services are not listed in Schedule 2 of the Environmental Law No. 4 of 1994, as amended by Law No. 9 of 2009
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or particulate discharge thresholds apply to the registered office activity; general office solid-waste handling must comply with the Waste Management Regulation Law No. 202 of 2020, and standby generator emissions, if installed, must meet the ambient air-quality limits of Law 4/1994; data-center e-waste disposal is reportable to the EEAA waste tracking system.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory Civil Defense fire-safety certificate for the registered office, including approved fire extinguishers, emergency exits and alarm systems; structural-load inspection report for the leased premises; occupational health and safety clearance under the Labor Law No. 12 of 2003 covering first-aid readiness, electrical safety, and workplace ergonomic compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Cairo, Egypt; unified electronic portal via https://eta.gov.eg and investment registration portal https://www.invest.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned LLC must first obtain a Tax Card (TIN) from the ETA by submitting the certified memorandum of association, articles of incorporation, board resolution appointing a local fiscal representative, power of attorney, notarized lease of registered office, and foreign shareholder identity documents. Registration is completed through the ETA online registration system, followed by an on-site inspection and issuance of the electronic Tax Card. For VAT, an additional VAT registration application (Form R-1) must be filed with the same portal; the ETA assigns the VAT ID and activation number. No minimum capital is required for the LLC, and volume of business is irrelevant for initial TIN registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not permit US-style check-the-box elections or hybrid mismatch elective classification. Available statutory elections include: (i) investment incentive election under the Investment Law No. 72/2017 (free-zone status with a 0% VAT and customs treatment; 50% reduction of corporate income tax on eligible sectoral activities); (ii) election of the Small and Medium Enterprise tax regime under Law No. 130/2023 for taxable turnover up to EGP 20 million (presumptive tax bands); and (iii) election to apply the General Tax Treaty transitional rules for qualifying foreign dividend and royalty flows. No pass-through election exists for an LLC.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax) pursuant to Law No. 67 of 2016 and its Executive Regulations
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover (mandatory registration threshold); EGP 1,000,000 threshold for voluntary registration during the first year of activity
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic invoicing and fiscal clearance. All tax invoices must be issued through the ETA-approved e-invoicing system (Rakia) via secured API integration; every invoice receives a unique QR code, online reference code, and ETA validation hash before being legally recognized. B2C sales additionally require e-receipts (E-Receipts) with the same real-time clearance protocol. Non-cleared invoices are treated as non-issued, triggering a penalty of EGP 50,000 per invoice in addition to reversals of input credit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and services are zero-rated under VAT Law No. 67 of 2016, Article 21 (goods) and Article 33 (services). To qualify for 0% VAT on programmatic advertising and DSP/SSP services, the LLC must demonstrate that: (i) the recipient is a non-resident person with no business establishment in Egypt; (ii) the service is not used, in whole or in part, for the recipient's taxable operations within Egypt; and (iii) the export proceeds are received in foreign currency in an Egyptian licensed bank account. The ETA applies the 'offshore benefit' test, requiring the ad inventory and targeting data to be consumed or utilized outside Egyptian territory. Merely issuing an invoice to a foreign entity is insufficient.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Genshiru) duly stamped by the Customs Authority (for goods; services are evidenced by a digital service export statement)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill (for physical goods) or a contract of cross-border service performance and the service delivery certificate
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by an Egyptian bank confirming receipt of foreign currency for the exported service
Copy of the VAT invoice zero-rated with encoded QR and ETA clearance reference
Board resolution confirming the transaction and the overseas ''use and benefit'' declaration
Forex repatriation declaration and statement of the credited foreign currency account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA may reopen and reassess VAT returns for a limitation period of up to five years (six years where intent to avoid tax is shown). Failure to produce the mandatory export documentation or failure to repatriate the foreign exchange within the 180-day deadline results in retroactive cancellation of the 0% treatment, immediate assessment of the applicable 14% VAT with interest computed at 2% per month from the invoice date, and a fine up to 100% of the tax evaded under VAT Law Articles 69–73. The submission of forged export documents or the use of shell invoices to fabricate export zero-rating is a criminal offence punishable by imprisonment and monetary penalties up to EGP 100,000 per invoice. Tax authorities will also claw back any previously refunded VAT input credit linked to the reversed zero-rating claim.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), acting under the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020, together with the banking, foreign-exchange, anti-money-laundering, payment-system, and export-control rules administered by the competent Egyptian authorities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Egyptian pound is generally usable for current-account transactions through licensed Egyptian banks, but practical convertibility is subject to CBE rules, bank liquidity, documentary controls, sanctions screening, and availability of foreign currency. Capital-account transactions, dividend remittances, shareholder-loan repayments, intercompany payments, and other outward transfers are not equivalent to unrestricted convertibility and may require evidence of source of funds, tax compliance, underlying contracts, corporate approvals, and bank-level CBE compliance review. A foreign-owned LLC may generally remit dividends and other lawful distributions after preparation of approved financial statements, satisfaction of applicable corporate-law requirements, settlement or provisioning of Egyptian taxes, and completion of the bank's purpose, beneficial-owner, and source-of-funds checks. Banks may defer or reject transfers where foreign currency is unavailable, the transaction is inadequately documented, the beneficiary or intermediary presents sanctions risk, or the transfer is inconsistent with the company's registered activity. The company should maintain a local-currency operating account and, where commercially justified and accepted by the bank, foreign-currency accounts for permitted receipts and payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Egypt does not generally impose a blanket rule requiring every exporter to convert a fixed percentage of export proceeds into Egyptian pounds. Export proceeds must be received through approved banking channels and supported by the relevant commercial, customs, shipping, and banking documentation. Timing and repatriation requirements may vary by export regime, product, free-zone or special-economic-zone status, customs treatment, financing structure, and current CBE or banking instructions. The company should obtain written confirmation from its relationship bank and the relevant customs or trade authority before commencing export activity. For an AdTech exchange or SSP platform, advertising and platform-service receipts are normally service receipts rather than goods-export proceeds; the company should preserve contracts, invoices, tax documents, platform reports, and foreign-inward-remittance evidence. No mandatory conversion ratio should be assumed without a transaction-specific bank confirmation. Any applicable export-receipt reporting, collection, repatriation, or conversion deadline should be documented in the bank's current operating instructions and monitored by treasury.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; foreign-currency account subject to bank approval; capital or investment-related account where required by the transaction structure
Operational Account; foreign-currency collection and payment account subject to documentary review; capital or investment-related account where applicable
Operational Account; foreign-currency account; dedicated collection or payment account subject to risk approval
Operational Account; foreign-currency account; treasury and hedging account subject to product eligibility and underlying-exposure evidence
Operational Account; foreign-currency account; trade-finance and treasury account subject to onboarding approval

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium for supplementary collections and payment orchestration, but Low for replacing an Egyptian bank account. An offshore digital EMI generally cannot independently provide an Egyptian local account, local-currency settlement, unrestricted Egyptian payment services, or a substitute for CBE-licensed banking and payment infrastructure. Use of an offshore EMI may be feasible for receiving or paying funds outside Egypt where its home-jurisdiction licence, Egyptian foreign-exchange rules, contractual terms, sanctions controls, and tax documentation permit the activity. The Egyptian LLC should not use personal wallets, unlicensed virtual accounts, informal netting, or an offshore account to circumvent CBE requirements. Customer-funds safeguarding, merchant acquiring, payment aggregation, remittance, and domestic payment activities may require licensing or regulated-bank sponsorship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no universal statutory rule that every director must appear physically at a bank branch for every corporate account opening. In practice, Egyptian banks commonly require certified corporate documents, specimen signatures, identification of directors and ultimate beneficial owners, tax and commercial-registration evidence, and enhanced verification for foreign shareholders or cross-border activity. Remote onboarding may be accepted in limited cases through bank-approved procedures, notarisation, consular legalisation, video verification, or an authorised signatory. A physical meeting, branch visit, local authorised signatory, or in-person verification may nevertheless be required by the selected bank, especially for foreign-owned entities, high-volume foreign-currency activity, new relationships, complex ownership, or treasury products.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign ownership, layered holding companies, nominee arrangements, or inability to identify the ultimate natural-person beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial registration; constitutional documents; complete ownership chart to natural-person UBOs; passports and residential-address evidence for UBOs, directors, and authorised signatories; shareholder registers; certificates of incorporation and good standing for foreign shareholders; board resolutions; notarised and legalised documents with Arabic translations where requested; independent corporate registry extracts; and a signed ownership and control certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Programmatic advertising model involving multiple advertisers, agencies, publishers, SSPs, DSPs, ad exchanges, payment processors, and automated settlement flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business memorandum; platform architecture; customer and counterparty taxonomy; standard advertiser, publisher, and exchange agreements; invoice and settlement-flow diagrams; sample campaign reports; revenue-recognition policy; refund and chargeback procedures; counterparties' jurisdiction and sanctions screening methodology; transaction-monitoring rules; and explanation of why the activity is not money transmission, deposit-taking, or unlicensed payment aggregation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large, rapid, or volatile foreign-currency inflows inconsistent with the company's paid-up capital, forecast revenue, staffing, or registered business profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved financial model; 12-month cash-flow forecast; signed commercial contracts; purchase orders; invoices; platform logs; advertising-spend and publisher-payout reconciliations; audited or management accounts; tax-registration evidence; source-of-funds certificates; bank statements; and written explanation of seasonality, campaign concentration, expected currencies, and transaction volumes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving high-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned persons, sanctioned sectors, virtual assets, mixers, privacy-enhancing tools, or opaque payment intermediaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty KYC files; beneficial-ownership evidence; sanctions and adverse-media screening records; country-risk assessment; payment-purpose memorandum; contractual restrictions on sanctioned activity; bank-approved correspondent route; transaction-monitoring alerts and disposition records; and documented prohibition of cash, cryptoasset, anonymous-wallet, and unapproved third-party settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign inbound capital described inconsistently as share capital, shareholder loan, service revenue, advance, or convertible instrument.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or loan agreement; shareholder and board resolutions; capitalisation table; investment registration or filing evidence where applicable; remittance instruction using the bank-approved purpose; source-of-funds evidence; accounting entries; tax analysis; and reconciliation between the incoming wire, corporate records, and regulatory filing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dividend, management-fee, royalty, interest, or intercompany payment to a non-resident without tax and transfer-pricing support.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved financial statements; distributable-profit calculation; shareholder resolution; tax-clearance or tax-payment evidence where requested; withholding-tax analysis; treaty-residency certificate; beneficial-ownership declaration; transfer-pricing documentation; intercompany agreement; proof of services or rights supplied; invoice; and arm's-length benchmarking.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, offshore wallets, payment aggregators, or third-party collection accounts for company receipts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy prohibiting personal and unapproved third-party accounts; bank-account mandate; approved payment-service-provider list; reconciliation controls; customer-payment instructions; exception register; remediation plan; and evidence that all historical receipts have been identified, documented, and regularised.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between ISIC or commercial-registration activity, tax profile, website description, and requested banking products.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated commercial-registration extract; tax-card and VAT-registration evidence where applicable; business licence or activity confirmation; Arabic and English business description; website and product screenshots; service agreements; management representation; and written bank confirmation of permitted account use.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High chargebacks, disputed card transactions, unexplained publisher credits, or negative balances in automated settlement accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chargeback and fraud policy; customer due-diligence standards; transaction-monitoring reports; reserve methodology; reconciliation files; publisher identity and payout verification; dispute correspondence; refund approvals; payment-processor reports; and evidence of segregation between customer funds and company funds where legally required.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder equity, paid-in capital, and shareholder loans through a bank licensed to operate in Egypt, from an account held in the documented name of the investor or lender. Use the bank-approved purpose and transaction narrative; do not describe an investment as service revenue or use an unrelated third-party remitter. Before remittance, provide the subscription, loan, or investment agreement, corporate approvals, ownership information, source-of-funds evidence, beneficiary account details, and any required investment, corporate, or regulatory filings. Use SWIFT MT103 or the bank's equivalent payment message with complete ordering-customer, beneficiary, purpose, and intermediary information. Reconcile the incoming amount to the general ledger, capitalisation table, loan schedule, and bank advice. Retain the SWIFT copy, credit advice, exchange-rate evidence, bank correspondence, and regulatory filings. Foreign-currency conversion should be performed only by the licensed bank and only after confirming the permitted account purpose and current CBE requirements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For legitimate cross-border service, technology, advertising, hosting, data, software, and vendor payments, use a licensed Egyptian bank and provide the underlying contract, invoice, tax and withholding analysis, proof of receipt or service, beneficiary ownership information, and any import, customs, or technology documentation required by the bank. SWIFT MT103 is appropriate for ordinary wire settlement; the payment message should identify the true beneficiary and commercial purpose. A Commercial Letter of Credit is generally relevant to documentary trade in goods and is not normally required for ordinary AdTech or digital-service payments. For goods transactions, use an irrevocable documentary commercial LC or documentary collection where commercially appropriate, with compliant invoices, transport documents, insurance documents, certificates of origin, customs records, and sanctions screening. Avoid informal netting, unapproved offsetting, cash settlement, cryptoasset settlement, and payment through unrelated third parties. Dividend and intercompany remittances require separate corporate, tax, transfer-pricing, and bank documentation and should not be processed as trade payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with a CBE-authorised bank, limited to supported currency pairs, documented commercial exposure, approved limits, and bank-required evidence of the underlying receivable or payable.

Foreign-exchange swaps with an authorised bank for short-term liquidity and currency-tenor management, subject to bank credit approval, documented business purpose, counterparty limits, and applicable CBE rules.

Currency swaps or cross-currency swaps may be available on a bilateral basis for material and documented exposures, subject to authorised-bank approval, master documentation, collateral or margin requirements, valuation controls, and legal review.

Non-deliverable forwards may be available only where the authorised bank offers the product and the transaction is permitted under current Egyptian rules. Availability, eligible currencies, settlement currency, underlying-exposure requirements, and accounting treatment must be confirmed in writing before execution; an NDF must not be used to evade Egyptian foreign-exchange controls.

Plain-vanilla FX options or option collars may be available only from an authorised bank and subject to suitability, documentation, accounting, premium-funding, and underlying-exposure controls. Complex or leveraged derivatives should be prohibited unless separately approved by the board and reviewed by legal, tax, risk, and treasury functions.

Treasury policy requirements should include board-approved counterparty limits, segregation of dealing and confirmation, independent valuation, hedge-designation records, maturity and notional limits, documentation of forecast versus committed exposure, collateral controls, sanctions screening, and monthly hedge-effectiveness and accounting review.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (unified tax return for legal persons)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the close of the fiscal year; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 30 April of the following year. Three interim advance CIT payments fall due in February, March and April before filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharge of 2% per month on the unpaid CIT plus interest at the statutory credit rate; fixed late-filing penalty in the EGP 1,000-5,000 range; enforced collection, seizure orders and criminal referral for repeat offenders; three consecutive years of non-filing exposes the company to administrative strike-off via the General Authority for Investment (GAFI).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT Reconciliation Return (annual declaration covering the 12 monthly returns)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of the end of the fiscal year; monthly VAT returns and payment must be submitted by the end of the month immediately following each tax month.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 2% monthly surcharge on unpaid VAT plus administrative late-filing fines per monthly return; continued default causes suspension of the tax card, blocking commercial registration renewal and triggering GAFI administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registration Renewal (data card renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Directorate, Ministry of Investment and Foreign Trade
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal window from 1 January to 31 March of each calendar year; any change of directors, managers or registered address must be filed within 15 days of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary fine per month of delay under the Commercial Registry Law; failure to renew for more than six months results in the registrar striking off the registration, causing the LLC to lose legal standing to contract or litigate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited Financial Statements and Annual Report to GAFI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary General Assembly must approve the audited financial statements within six months of fiscal year-end and the stamped audited financial statements must be lodged with GAFI within 20 days of approval; practically by 31 July for a 31 December year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under the Companies Law of up to EGP 50,000; failure to deposit financial statements for two consecutive years enables GAFI to commence administrative strike-off after formal notice and publication in the official gazette.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) confirmation and shareholding register update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) / Egyptian AML Financial Intelligence Unit (FRCU)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual UBO confirmation within 30 days of the fiscal year-end (31 January for a December year-end); any transfer of membership interest or change in control must be notified within 30 days of completion.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML Law 80/2002 fines of up to EGP 500,000 for entities and personal criminal liability for managers who knowingly conceal UBO data; non-confirmation blocks all GAFI licenses and annual renewals and forms grounds for suspension of registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is mandatory for every Egyptian LLC irrespective of revenue or headcount: at least one independent auditor licensed by the Egyptian Tax Authority must be appointed by the General Assembly each year; there is no size-based audit exemption under Companies Law 159/1981.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), issued by Ministry of Finance Decree No. 407/2015 and closely converged with IFRS, are mandatory for statutory books and financial statements; the ETA also requires books to be maintained on the accrual basis for CIT and VAT purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must maintain a UBO register identifying every natural person ultimately owning or controlling more than 25% of the membership interests or voting power. An annual confirmation of the UBO list must be lodged with GAFI within 30 days of the fiscal year-end and re-filed within 30 days whenever shares are transferred or control changes; non-resident assignees are equally reportable and the register is available for inspection by the FRCU on request.
